items.evidence: After a page.reload() the test checks that statusInfo reads "Cancelled" and that the fulfil button is gone (diff lines 77-80). Both would fail if the cancel mutation never ran.
All three criteria are asserted: status "Cancelled" (line 71), no fulfil action (line 72), and status still "Cancelled" after reload (lines 77-79).

The new moreActionsButton and cancelOrderMenuItem fields go on the existing OrderPage. No equivalent locators or a cancel helper exist yet in e2e/pages, e2e/lib or e2e/scenarios. findOrderId and ORDERS_SCENARIO are reused.
No waitForTimeout, sleeps or polling loops.
test and expect are imported from fixtures/test.ts, the test is not tagged parallel(), and nothing writes to the cache or dumps.
Locators use test ids and roles. The header trigger is scoped to page-header and the dialog's submit/back buttons are scoped to orderPage.dialog.
Uses the orders scenario's existing unpaid order through findOrderId and creates no data.
No hard-coded ids. The order is looked up by its scenario key, and the dialog text check only matches the static prefix "Cancel order #".
Uses the default admin stored session with no UI sign-in, which suits a ticket that names no specific permission.
The type check exits 0 with no errors, and the spec is at e2e/tests/orders/order-cancel.spec.ts.

e2e/tests/orders/order-cancel.spec.ts diff lines 43 and 51-66: the confirm-button locator (dialog.getByTestId("submit")), page.getByRole("menu") and the whole multi-step cancel flow are written inline in the spec instead of as a cancel method on OrderPage (like markAsPaid).
The new members are readonly fields initialised from this.page on a class that already uses constructor(readonly page: Page) {}.
The spec has // Arrange, // Act and // Assert comments.
One test covers the story, with a test.step for each stage.
The title "Cancel an unpaid, unfulfilled order #e2e" describes the behaviour and carries the tag.
A doc comment at the top of the spec (diff lines 31-35) says what it covers and why it uses the scenario.
All assertions are web-first expect(locator) calls.

The scenario name comes from ORDERS_SCENARIO and the order from its typed key "unpaid", as in the existing specs. Status strings are literal UI labels, which matches the suite's habit. No money is compared.
No cleanup code and no unique names.
No per-test timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState.
Relative imports keep the .ts extension, and test/expect come only from the fixture.
No any, no casts and no gql calls.

e2e/tests/orders/order-cancel.spec.ts diff lines 23-24, 45, 52, 63, 70 and 76: generated boilerplate ("// spec: specs/order-cancel.md", "// seed: ...") and numbered step comments ("// 2. Click \"More actions\"...", "// 5. Reload and check again") narrate the next lines instead of explaining why.

structured_output.summary: The change is solid on every blocker. It reuses the scenario's unpaid order, scopes its locators properly, type-checks, and checks after a reload that the order is cancelled and the fulfil action is gone, so it would fail if the cancel mutation never ran. Two minors fail. The cancel flow and the dialog/menu locators are written inline in the spec instead of as a cancel method on OrderPage. The spec also carries generated boilerplate and numbered comments that narrate the steps.
